newsitem.title: KENYA: Exporter sales push Kenyan shilling up.
newsitem.headline: Exporter sales push Kenyan shilling up.

text.p: Money from exporter sales continued to flow into the market, pushing the Kenyan shilling two cents up against the dollar on Monday, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean rate of 55.38 shillings to the dollar, from 55.40 on Friday, while on sterling it was posted at 93.29, from 93.04.
"Exporter sales put pressure on the dollar, pushing it downwards," one dealer said.
Some dealers said trade opened at 55.38/43 and broke the 55.40 barrier to trade at 55.32/37.

"The market is very subdued. Most customers are slowly drifting away, possibly because Christmas is just around the corner and they are looking to honour their commitments," one commercial dealer said.
"In fact we have seen the rates stuck at 55.35/40 this morning," he added
The money market was very liquid, with many banks lending. Overnight rates remained below 10 percent levels.
